intro:
Use it to show what a total over time is made of: sessions by channel, revenue by plan. Each row of `data` is a point, and each `AreaChart.Area` is a band drawn from one of its keys.

With `stacked`, each band sits on the ones below it, so the top edge is the total and each thickness is a share. Without it the bands overlay, for series that are alternatives rather than parts.

The grid, the axes, the legend and the readout are separate parts, so a chart has only the ones you write.

For one series where the shape matters more than what it is made of, use a line chart instead.
usage:
<AreaChart data={traffic} xDataKey="hour" stacked>
  <AreaChart.Grid />
  <AreaChart.Area dataKey="direct" />
  <AreaChart.Area dataKey="search" color="chart-2" />
  <AreaChart.XAxis />
  <AreaChart.Tooltip />
</AreaChart>

parts.Header: The strip above the plot: `title`, `value` and `caption`, with the series key or your own control on the trailing side.
parts.Grid: Lines across the value axis, in the theme's border colour. `rows` is roughly how many: the axis picks round numbers near it.
parts.Area: One filled band with a line along its top edge. Declare one per key. In a stack, the first is the bottom.
parts.Line: A series drawn as a line with no fill, over the bands. It is never part of a stack, counts toward the value axis and has a row in the readout. `curve="step"` holds each value until the next.
parts.ReferenceLine: A rule across the plot at the value `y`: a budget, a limit, a target. `label` writes text above its left end.
parts.Marker: A rule down the plot at the row `index`: a release, the day something ran out. `label` writes text beside its top.
parts.Skeleton: A low band on the baseline with a highlight moving across it, drawn only while `status` is `loading`.
parts.XAxis: The x labels, each on its own point. Labels are dropped when they get too close. `ticks` asks for fewer, evenly spaced with both ends kept.
parts.YAxis: Value labels on the grid lines, in round numbers, with room made for them.
parts.Legend: A swatch and a name per series, over the top corner of the plot, reversed for a stack so it reads in the order the bands appear. On a chart with a header, use the header's `legend` prop instead.
parts.Labels: The value at the end of each series, beside where that series ends. Below 32rem of width they wrap under the plot. `extra` adds a figure that belongs to no one series.
parts.Tooltip: The readout, and what drives it. It adds the crosshair and a dot on every band's top edge, and it covers the plot, so the pointer can be anywhere. `labels` names the series in it.

examples.title: Overlaid
examples.description: Leave out `stacked` when the series are alternatives, such as two plans compared. The fills go translucent so each band shows through the other, and a later `Area` draws over an earlier one.

examples.title: Reading it without hovering
examples.description: `Line` draws a series outside the stack, such as income above what was spent. `Labels` writes each series' last value beside it. `ReferenceLine` marks a value and `Marker` marks a row.

examples.title: Tuning the fill
examples.description: `fillOpacity` is the weight at the top of a band and `gradientToOpacity` the weight at the bottom. Matching them gives a flat fill. `showLine={false}` drops the edge.

examples.title: Picking out a series
examples.description: `opacity` fades a whole series, fill and edge, and its entry in `Labels` fades with it. `onSelect` reports the `Area` chosen on the plot or in `Labels`, so state can drive it. Here each series also has a colour of its own.

examples.title: Loading, then data
examples.description: Add `AreaChart.Skeleton` and drive `status`. The bands grow out of the baseline when it turns `ready`. Without the skeleton the plot is empty while loading.

examples.title: Changing data
examples.description: When `data` changes, the bands and the axis move to their new values over `domainDuration`. A `ref` on the chart has `replay()`, which grows the bands in again.

notes:
### Stacked or overlaid

Stack when the series are parts of one thing and the total means something: channels making up your traffic, plans making up your revenue. Overlay when a total would mean nothing: two plans compared.

The chart does not add up a stack's total for you. The first example works it out from the row that `onActiveIndexChange` passes.

### The baseline

The derived value axis always includes zero, because an area floating above the bottom of the plot reads as a shape rather than a quantity. `yDomain` fixes the axis to other values.

### Gaps

A missing value leaves a gap in its own band. In a stack it counts as zero for the bands above it.

### Sizing

The chart fills its container's width and takes its height from `aspectRatio`, which applies to the plot alone, so a header does not shrink it. The plot draws in the browser after it has been measured, and the space is reserved until then, so it is not in server-rendered HTML.

### Bundle size

The chart adds about 67 KB of gzipped JavaScript to a page that uses it. A page that does not import it pays nothing, including one that imports other components from the package root.

### Colour

`color` names a role in the theme. Every `Area` defaults to `chart-1`, so give the others their own. `Line` and `ReferenceLine` default to `foreground`, and `Marker` to `muted-foreground`. `color` also takes any CSS colour, for a colour that comes from your data. Unlike a role, it does not change with the theme.

### Reading a point

With a `Tooltip`, hovering the plot reads the nearest point. A click or a tap pins the reading until the next press elsewhere, or Escape. On a touch screen a sideways drag reads the points it crosses, and a vertical drag scrolls the page.

`onActiveIndexChange` fires when the point changes, not on every frame, so it can drive a readout outside the chart, as the first example does. Inside the chart, `useAreaChart` gives the same point.

### Keyboard

With a `Tooltip`, the plot takes focus. The arrow keys move between points, Home and End go to the first and last, Enter or Space pins the reading, and Escape clears it.

The arrow keys move between rows, not series, so Enter on the plot does not call `onSelect`. Add `AreaChart.Labels` so a keyboard can reach it: each `Area`'s entry becomes a button.

### Screen readers

Each row is given as text beside the drawing. `label` names the chart and `labelForDatum` writes a row, for values with a unit. Without them a row is read as its keys and values.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion set, the bands and the axis appear at their final values, and the skeleton's highlight is not drawn.
propsNote: `AreaChart`, `AreaChart.Header`, `AreaChart.Legend` and `AreaChart.Labels` also take the props of the element they render, and a `className`. `AreaChart.Tooltip` puts its `className` on the readout. The other parts draw nothing themselves and take only the props listed.
